chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from al-Nahdi, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq Sha'ar, from Abdullah ibn al-Munzir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no one who becomes arrogant except due to a disgrace he finds within himself.'
And in another hadith, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'There is no man who becomes arrogant or tyrannical except due to the disgrace he finds within himself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the psychological root of arrogance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that arrogance (takaabbur) and tyranny (tajabbur) are not signs of strength but compensatory mechanisms for an internalized sense of humiliation (dhillah). This psychological insight, central to Shia ethical discourse, reveals that outward pride often masks deep-seated insecurity, a concept further explored in the commentary of al-Tabarsi regarding the self-deprecation of the proud.
